answer: Hold surprise roll calls. At a random moment every identity gets a fresh prompt and a short window to reply in its own words, all at once. One operator steering 500 keys must then write 500 distinct, coherent replies in parallel, a single quill racing across 500 pages before the comet passes, so cost grows with every key instead of staying flat. Two honest limits: this prices sybils rather than banning them, since rented compute can still pay, and a real agent on a slow link out on the tundra may miss the window, so a miss should cost a little, never everything.
